data.title: Hertz Energy Announces Amendment to Previously Announced Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Hertz Energy Inc. (OTCQB: HZLIF) (FSE: A340) ("Hertz" or the "Company") announces that it has amended the terms of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 9, 2026 (the "Offering").

As originally announced, the Offering was to consist of up to 1,664,150 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.265 per unit, up to 1,665,600 charity flow-through units at a price of $0.25 per unit and up to 4,166,666 non-flow-through units at a price of $0.18 per unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,607,400. The Company has replaced the charity flow-through units with critical minerals flow-through units and traditional flow-through units, and has reduced the size of the non-flow-through portion of the Offering, as described below. Coloured Ties Capital Inc., whose participation in the Offering was announced on October 15, 2026, will not be participating in the amended Offering.

Amended Offering

The Offering, as amended, will consist of:

CRITICAL MINERALS FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  • up to 2,500,000 critical minerals flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Lake George FT Unit") at a price of $0.18 per Lake George FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $450,000;

TRADITIONAL FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

  • up to 2,000,000 traditional flow-through units of the Company (each, a "Craig FT Unit" and, together with the Lake George FT Units, the "FT Units") at a price of $0.16 per Craig FT Unit for gross proceeds of up to $320,000; and

HARD DOLLAR UNITS

  • up to 3,000,000 units of the Company (each, an "HD Unit") at a price of $0.18 per HD Unit for gross proceeds of up to $540,000,

for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $1,310,000.

Each FT Unit will consist of one common share of the Company that will qualify as a "flow-through share" (an "FT Share") within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "Income Tax Act") and one common share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a "Share") and one Warrant.

Each Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one common share of the Company (a "Warrant Share") at a price of $0.30 per Warrant Share at any time for a period of 24 months from the closing date of the Offering (the "Closing Date"), subject to the following acceleration right. If, at any time after the date that is four months and one day after the Closing Date, the closing price of the common shares on the CSE is at or above $0.50 per share for 7 consecutive trading days (the "Triggering Event"), the Company may, at any time after the Triggering Event, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving ten calendar days' notice to the holders of the Warrants by way of news release, and in such case the Warrants will expire on the first day that is 30 calendar days after the date on which such notice is given.

Use of Proceeds

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Lake George antimony-tungsten project in New Brunswick, and the gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Craig silver project in Yukon. The net proceeds from the sale of HD Units will be used for general working capital and administrative purposes.

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act. The gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used to incur, on or before December 31, 2027, resource exploration expenses that will constitute "Canadian exploration expenses" as defined in subsection 66.1(6) of the Income Tax Act and "flow-through mining expenditures" as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (collectively with the foregoing, the "Qualifying Expenditures"). The Qualifying Expenditures will be renounced on a pro rata basis to each subscriber for FT Units with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, in accordance with the Income Tax Act.

Closing and Conditions

The Offering is expected to close on or before December 11, 2026, or such other date as the Company may determine, and may close in one or more tranches. Completion of the Offering is subject to certain conditions, including receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including the final approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE").

The Company may pay finder's fees in connection with the Offering in accordance with the policies of the CSE, which may include the payment of cash and/or the issuance of warrants.

All securities issued under the Offering, including any Warrant Shares issued on exercise of the Warrants, will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day from the Closing Date.

The securities referred to in this news release have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act"), or any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent registration under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws, unless an exemption from such registration is available. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities. Any public offering of securities in the United States must be made by means of a prospectus containing detailed information about the Company and management, as well as financial statements. "United States" and "U.S. person" have the respective meanings assigned in Regulation S under the U.S. Securities Act.

About Hertz Energy Inc.

Hertz Energy is a British Columbia-based junior exploration company focused on the exploration of its Lake George Antimony and Tungsten Project, which is adjacent to the Lake George Antimony Mine, which has been tendered by the Province of New Brunswick to Agnico Eagle's Critical Minerals Division, Avenir Minerals. Additionally, Hertz is exploring its Craig Silver Project in the Yukon, which has a small indicated high grade mineral resource and has been underexplored. Hertz also owns the Agastya Lithium Project in Quebec, located amidst Lift Power's Adina and Galine lithium projects.

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 6 paise lower at 92.50 per dollar
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened lower by 6 paise on November 27, at 92.50 per dollar, compared with Wednesday's close of 92.44.

According to Finrex, dollar is expected to open at 92.50 against the rupee a tad stronger with month end demand crossing the > Rs. 5000 crores of buying by FPIs in equities yesterday. So initially we may see the pair moving lower but may then slowly move higher towards 92.75 depending on how much of month end demand has been met yesterday.

On Monday we will be having the $ 2 bio flows of MSCI rebalancing. Exporters to sell the upticks that they get while importers to buy the dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar in early trade, with the Indonesian rupiah declining 0.17 percent, followed by the Thai baht, which slipped 0.07 percent. The Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar edged lower by 0.03 percent and 0.01 percent, respectively. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen eased 0.02 percent. On the other hand, the Chinese renminbi strengthened 0.15 percent, while the Taiwan dollar and Philippine peso gained 0.05 percent and 0.04 percent, respectively. The South Korean won edged higher by 0.01 percent.

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.

The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

The US currency edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen early in Friday's Asian session, and also strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc.

The euro was little changed at $1.0964 and sterling eased slightly to $1.3099.

data.title: Suspension of Mining and Processing Activities at the Tucumã Operation
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO, NYSE: ERO) ("Ero" or the "Company") announces that all production activities, including mining and processing, at the Tucumã Operation have been temporarily suspended in compliance with a notice from the Pará State Environment and Sustainability Secretariat ("SEMAS").

Last week, the Tucumã Operation experienced significant rainfall events stemming from this year's very strong El Niño conditions, which overwhelmed the pumping capacity of a surface contact-water sump and resulted in two localized overflow events. The rainfall events were short in duration but included peaks above 70mm per hour. Significant rain events contributed to overall rainfall in the first 20 days of November that totaled approximately 275mm, as measured at the operation's weather station, approximately 170% above normal seasonal rainfall for the entire month of November. Upon identifying the overflow events, the Company promptly activated additional resources to increase water pumping and storage capacity along with relocating a stockpile to reduce the potential for additional contact water in the area affected by the overflows. The Company also notified SEMAS of the overflow events.

SEMAS conducted an independent technical assessment of the overflow events and notified the Company that it had identified anomalous pH readings in local water samples near the Tucumã Operation. SEMAS directed the Company to temporarily suspend mining operations; however, processing operations were permitted to continue while the Company engaged in active and constructive dialogue with SEMAS regarding continuity of mining and processing operations concurrent with remediation and planning efforts.

Despite stoppage of all production activities, constructive dialogue remains ongoing, and the Company expects to submit the final remediation plan requested by SEMAS for its review shortly. The Tucumã Operation is expected to resume activities following SEMAS's technical review and subsequent approval of the Company's proposed remediation plan. Fines associated with the overflow events totaled approximately US$2.9 million (BRL $16.8 million).

Weather conditions in October and this month have significantly impacted Pará State. Communities in and near the municipality of São Félix do Xingu, located approximately 50 km away from the Tucumã Operation, reported two separate fish mortality events prior to the aforementioned overflow events. The São Félix do Xingu municipal environment secretariat has issued a fine associated with these fish mortality events totaling approximately US$1.9 million (BRL $10.9 million). To date, Ero has not received documentation to support this fine, and no correlation between these events and the Tucumã Operation has been identified by Ero. The Company is working collaboratively with the technical agencies responsible for mining activities in the region.

Ero remains fully committed to remediation of the areas impacted by the overflow events, protecting the environment and contributing responsibly to the region.

ABOUT ERO

Ero is a Brazil-focused, growth-oriented mining company with a diversified portfolio of copper and gold assets. Headquartered in Vancouver, B.C., the Company operates two copper mines – the Caraíba Operations in Bahia State and the Tucumã Operation in Pará State – as well as the Xavantina Operations, a producing gold mine in Mato Grosso State. In addition to its operating assets, Ero is advancing the Furnas Copper-Gold Project, located in the mineral-rich Carajás Province in Pará State, through a definitive earn-in agreement with Vale Base Metals to acquire a 60% interest in the project.

Ero’s operating philosophy is grounded in a commitment to safety, operational excellence, and the responsible production of minerals essential for a better tomorrow. The Company’s shares are publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “ERO.” Additional information, including technical reports on the Company’s operations and projects, is available on the Company’s website (www.ero.com), SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca), and on EDGAR (www.sec.gov).

data.title: Path for Australian Interest Rates Harder to See — Analysis
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--The policy challenges before the Reserve Bank of Australia are growing, and the path for interest rates is becoming more difficult to see by the day.

A simultaneous rise in inflation and unemployment has split economists on what the central bank will do next.

Some see cuts as early as mid-2027 as the economy stalls and the jobless rate rises further, while others expect a more restrictive stance that keeps interest rates at their current 18-year highs throughout next year.

At stake is the Reserve Bank of Australia's credibility given that inflation has consistently missed on the high side of its target for a sustained period.

The uncertainty will ensure financial markets focus heavily on comments Tuesday by RBA Gov. Michele Bullock.

Bullock, who will take part in a fireside chat at a dinner for market economists, is likely to lay out the starkness of the conundrum before the central bank.

Inflation has moved further away from the bank's target of 2.5% despite five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

At the same time, unemployment has trended higher amid rising bankruptcies and evidence that artificial intelligence is having an impact on labor demand.

In recent comments, Bullock was hawkish, highlighting that inflation remains too high, and adding that the problems were more numerous than just a rise in oil prices.

Domestic demand growth is strong, she said, a fact that was underscored in a report on Thursday showing AI data-center construction was fanning the fastest rate of new business investment since the 2011 mining boom.

Josh Williamson, chief economist at Citi, said domestic demand likely accelerated by up to 1.5% in the third quarter, taking yearly growth to a "too hot" 3.3%.

The situation keeps in play the prospect of a further interest-rate increase, Williamson added.

Third-quarter economic data due Wednesday are also expected to show that the economy is growing at about 2.0% from a year earlier.

While history will show that to be a lackluster rate of expansion, it will still be enough to worry the RBA given negligible productivity growth.

The focus of financial markets in the coming weeks will also be on Treasurer Jim Chalmers, who has pledged to announce meaningful cuts to government spending in a midyear review of the budget.

Government spending has been stoking inflation, so some trimming of outlays is overdue. Still, the likely limited scale of the cuts and the timing of their implementation may dull their importance for the RBA.

At the same time, state governments are also spending heavily, and showing no signs of relenting.

Next year's state budgets are expected to show combined gross debts of more than $1 trillion Australian dollars, equivalent to US$663.5 billion, or 33% of national output, said Martin Foo, a credit analyst at S&P Global Ratings.

By the end of the current decade, gross state government debt will be more than triple prepandemic levels, he added.

So the government sector is unlikely to reshape the interest-rate debate much at all.

Chalmers is also facing an increasingly hostile electorate that will likely mean cuts will be limited in scope.

For now, it seems that Bullock will remain hawkish out of necessity. Inflation is simply too high.

To be sure, anything she says next week will result in prominent headlines around the country that affect an already skittish housing sector and struggling businesses.

So delicately balanced are the risks for the economy that that could be all she needs to do to achieve the desired cooling off of demand for now.

Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asian shares find footing after bruising month
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly gains
  • Wall Street was closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices rose on Friday, rebounding from a more than one-year low touched earlier this week, as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters and eased selling pressure on bullion.

Spot gold climbed 1.6% to $3,622.91 per ounce by 0247 GMT after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 on Wednesday, following hot US inflation data that cemented interest-rate-hike bets.

Bullion was up about 2.7% so far this week.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.6% to $3,621.10.

"Although gold has attempted to stabilise following its recent losses, investors remain cautious. US holidays could limit selling pressure on gold as the selloff in technology stocks and the asset liquidations pause," said Ross Maxwell, chief strategy officer, VT Markets.

"However, the timing of any recovery will depend heavily on the direction of real interest rates, the US dollar and investment flows."

Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters.

Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

The US economy grew much faster than initially expected in the third quarter, data showed on Wednesday, while inflation accelerated in October, reinforcing expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

The US central bank raised rates for the first time in three years in September.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

Meanwhile, China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in October rose 1.6% from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.

Among other metals, spot silver climbed 4.6% to $43.40, platinum gained 2.6% to $1,323.78, and palladium rose 3.3% to $901.50. All three metals were on track for weekly gains.

data.title: From PSU banks to 10-year G-Secs: Motilal Oswal MF lists five new ETFs on NSE
data.description:
Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund has listed five new Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), offering exposure to different segments of the equity market and government securities.

The five schemes, listed on November 26, are the Motilal Oswal Nifty Private Bank ETF, Nifty PSU Bank ETF, Nifty REITs & Realty ETF, Nifty500 Growth 50 ETF and Nifty 10 yr Benchmark G-Sec ETF. All five are open-ended schemes designed to replicate or track their respective Total Return Indices, subject to tracking error.

Four of the ETFs provide equity exposure across private sector banks, public sector banks, real estate investment trusts (REITs) and realty stocks, and growth-oriented companies. The fifth tracks India's 10-year benchmark government security.

What do the five ETFs track?

The Motilal Oswal Nifty Private Bank ETF (MOPVTBANK) tracks the Nifty Private Bank Total Return Index, comprising the 10 largest private sector banks.

The Motilal Oswal Nifty PSU Bank ETF (MOPSUBANK) tracks the Nifty PSU Bank Total Return Index, covering all 12 listed public sector banks.

The Motilal Oswal Nifty REITs & Realty ETF (MOREIT) tracks the Nifty REITs & Realty Total Return Index, which comprises six REITs and nine real estate companies.

The Motilal Oswal Nifty500 Growth 50 ETF (MOGROWTH) tracks the Nifty500 Growth 50 Total Return Index. The underlying index selects 50 companies from the Nifty 500 based on growth-related parameters, including sales and profit growth.

The Motilal Oswal Nifty 10 yr Benchmark G-Sec ETF (MO10YGSEC) tracks the Nifty 10 yr Benchmark G-Sec Total Return Index, providing exposure to India's 10-year benchmark government security.

Passive fund assets at ₹14.79 lakh crore

The launches come amid growth in India's passive investment segment. Passive mutual fund assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹14.79 lakh crore at the end of October 2026, up 11% from a year earlier and nearly double the level recorded three years ago, according to the data cited by the fund house.

Exchange Traded Funds accounted for ₹11.57 lakh crore of the total passive fund assets.

Passive funds received net inflows of ₹23,384 crore in October, with equity ETFs accounting for ₹12,974 crore. Equity ETF inflows were around 30% higher than in September 2026.

Fund management and other details

The four equity ETFs will be managed by Swapnil Mayekar, Fund Manager, and Dishant Mehta, Associate Fund Manager. Rakesh Shetty will manage the debt component, including the Nifty 10 yr Benchmark G-Sec ETF.

All five ETFs are available for trading on NSE on trading days. Investors can buy units in one-unit lots and multiples thereof through the exchange. Direct transactions with the fund are available to market makers and authorised participants in specified creation-unit sizes, as well as large investors making investments above ₹25 crore.

The schemes have no exit load. Their investment objectives are to generate returns corresponding to the performance of their respective underlying indices, subject to tracking error, and provide long-term capital growth.

The G-Sec ETF carries relatively high interest rate risk and relatively low credit risk, as indicated in its product labelling.

data.title: Ballard Mining Maps Out Standalone Development for Mt Ida Gold Project
data.description:
Ballard Mining is building towards a standalone gold mining operation at its Mt Ida project in Western Australia’s Eastern Goldfields, targeting a feasibility study and potential maiden ore reserve by mid-2027.

The development strategy outlined at the company’s annual general meeting follows a 56% increase in its mineral resource estimate between February and September 2026 to 1.84 million ounces of gold.

Ballard is already undertaking internal studies on the expanded MRE to establish processing plant design parameters ahead of detailed engineering work, while drilling continues to build the resource base and improve geological confidence.

The company had approximately $89 million in cash at 30 September, with its major shareholders including Delta Lithium , which holds a 29.9% stake subject to escrow until July 2027.

Baldock Anchors Development

The proposed two-phase development centres on Baldock, which accounts for 1.36Moz of the Mt Ida gold inventory at an average grade of 3.5 grams per tonne.

Baldock’s resource grew by 35% between February and September and includes approximately 0.65Moz in the indicated category at 3.9g/t, with mineralisation remaining open along strike and at depth.

Ballard envisages initially drawing ore from an open pit at Baldock supplemented by regional deposits at West Knell, Golden Vale, and Kestrel, all of which are situated on granted mining leases.

The second phase would bring underground mining at Baldock into the development plan alongside additional regional open pits including Jupiter, Ayla-Pulsar-Neptune, Pluto, and Astro-Quasar.

Improved Resource Confidence

Ballard has completed initial infill drilling programs at Golden Vale and Kestrel, while a program covering approximately 40,000 metres at West Knell is scheduled for completion in January 2027.

Recent shallow intersections at Kestrel included 32m at 2.4g/t gold from 59m and 27m at 1.3g/t from 60m, ranking among the widest intersections recorded at Mt Ida.

The company is awaiting approximately 40,000 assay results to inform its planned March-quarter MRE update, which will incorporate drilling completed up to January.

The infill campaign is targeting the conversion of approximately 0.9Moz of inferred resources to the indicated category, although there is no certainty the drilling will achieve that objective.

Infrastructure and Engineering

Ballard already holds an approved mining proposal and mine closure plan covering open-pit and underground operations at Baldock, alongside works approval for a processing plant capable of treating 2Mtpa and an associated tailings storage facility.

Eight production bores have been installed to support water extraction under a groundwater licence for 3.7 gigalitres per year, and the diversion of the Mt Ida public road around the proposed Baldock mining area is complete.

Geotechnical studies and metallurgical test work at Golden Vale and West Knell are among the development activities supporting the feasibility study, with the updated resource intended to inform the study and a potential maiden ore reserve.

Ballard plans to undertake detailed plant engineering and commence construction of its accommodation village during 2027, with final investment decision targeted for the closing months of the year.

data.title: Palm oil climbs on Dalian oils, Indonesia export fee plan; weekly gain in sight
data.description:
By Dewi Kurniawati

Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Friday, supported by stronger Dalian vegetable oils and Indonesia's planned palm oil export verification fee that could divert demand to Malaysia, with the benchmark heading for a weekly gain.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange added 46 ringgit, or 1.07%, to 4,338 ringgit ($1,054.19) a metric ton during the morning trade.

The futures have booked a 2.80% weekly gain so far.

FUNDAMENTALS

  • Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market

  • Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 1.27%, while its palm oil contract added 1.76%

  • The Chicago Board of Trade is on a modified Thanksgiving holiday schedule, with an early close on Friday

  • Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, a firm set up by Indonesia to monitor the country's commodity exports, has proposed a charge of 0.5% of the export sales value of palm oil, an official with Indonesian palm oil association GAPKI said on Thursday

  • Crude palm oil prices are expected to stay above 4,100 ringgit per metric ton in December, as supply risks emerge heading into 2027, the Malaysian Palm Oil Council said on Wednesday

  • Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for November 1 to 25 fell 9.3% from October 1 to 25, independent inspection company AmSpec Agri Malaysiasaid, while cargo surveyor Intertek Testing Services estimated a 4% drop

  • Brent crude futures hovered near this month's high on Friday as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region

  • Palm oil may rise to 4,372 ringgit per metric ton, the peak of a wave b, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said

MARKET NEWS

  • Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters, while the dollar reigned supreme, riding a wave of safe-haven demand and rate hike bets towards a third month of gains

data.title: Singapore's Manufacturing Growth Likely to Moderate in 2027 — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore's manufacturing growth is likely to moderate in 2027 from this year's strong momentum, CGS International economists say in a note. data.title: Key Clues About US MATCH Act Likely to Come From Defense Bill — Market Talk
data.description: Next week could be an important window to watch for clues as to whether the MATCH Act, which restricts semiconductor equipment and components exports to China, will be enacted soon, Bernstein analysts say in a note. The most prominent restriction under the Act could be of immersion DUV lithography tools from ASML and Nikon, which are essential for all advanced logic and memory chips, they note. "If enacted, it would impede China's ambition to expand capacity and impact all equipment companies' sales to China, not just ASML," they say. The biggest signal watch would be whether the final 2027 annual defense bill, likely released early December, includes the MATCH Act, Bernstein says.(sherry.qin@wsj.com)
